messages:
lucas: Heads up — our tiny widget bundle went +470KB after bumping @redwood/inference-js from 2.1.3 -> 2.2.0 and Vercel Edge started throwing "createClient is not a function" at runtime. Weirdly it only happens when deployed to Edge, local SSR works fine.

neha: do you have the import lines? default vs named can change how bundlers handle the package.

lucas: one-liner in utils: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js'`. Replacing with `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js'` made the runtime error go away in some builds but bundle size stayed large. Analyzer flags `node_modules/@redwood/inference-js/dist/cjs` in the output.

toni: possible causes: 1) package.json sideEffects flag hiding a boot file, 2) ESM entry wrapping a CJS default via interop helper, 3) exports mapping confusing bundler resolution. Can you paste package.json snippet?

lucas: pasted: 
```
{
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "dist/esm/index.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "exports": {
    ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
    "./boot": { "import": "./dist/esm/boot.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/boot.js" }
  }
}
```

sam: that `boot` file is likely doing tiny runtime wiring (fetch polyfill + global init). With sideEffects:false bundlers assume imports are pure and may drop `boot.js` unless referenced. If the ESM entry re-exports default from CJS via a shim, it can pull the cjs output in and also drop boot file — two bad outcomes.

neha: interesting nuance: Vite (esbuild) will prefer the `import` path but some plugin chains still include commonjs interop helpers when the published ESM file was built by bundling tools that left those helpers inline. Those helpers defeat tree-shaking and also create synthetic default exports that don't match names (hence createClient missing).

toni: consumer workaround that worked for me elsewhere: import directly from the ESM subpath `@redwood/inference-js/esm` or reference the boot path to ensure it's included, e.g. `import '@redwood/inference-js/boot'` early in your app. Ugly but effective.

lucas: tried both: `import '@redwood/inference-js/boot'` forces boot into bundle and fixes runtime, `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js/esm'` shrinks bundle but breaks TS resolution in our monorepo unless we add path alias. Neither is good for onboarding.

package-bot: NOTE: SDK was published with rollup config that inlines createCommonjsModule helper into the `dist/esm` build in 2.2.0. This makes ESM entry non-ideal for packagers.

neha: action items for SDK team: 1) either remove `sideEffects:false` or add "./dist/esm/boot.js" (and any other runtime mutators) to `sideEffects` allowlist; 2) publish a pure ESM entry that doesn't re-export CJS via interop shims; 3) make runtime-init explicit (export init function) so consumers opt-in; 4) verify published `.d.ts` references match the ESM layout so TS tooling doesn't break when files are pruned.

sam: created a minimal repro: https://gist.github.com/lucas/edge-esm-repro (contains Vite config + tiny app). Steps: install 2.2.0, default import, build, deploy to Vercel Edge -> error.

ci-bot: Ticket INF-3490 opened: "js-sdk: ESM/CJS interop + sideEffects false causes edge runtime failure and bundle bloat" assigned to eng-devex.

toni: short-term guidance for app teams: pin to 2.1.x, or explicitly import the boot file in your app, or use the explicit ESM subpath if you can update TS config. We'll add a troubleshooting snippet to the upgrade guide and examples repo.

neha: long-term: add automated tests that publish the package to a temp registry and run small consumer builds (vite/webpack/rollup) targeting node/edge to catch regressions before release. Also include a smoke test that runs the built artifact in a lightweight edge-like runtime.

lucas: thanks everyone — pinned the package and added the boot import for now. I'll watch INF-3490. :thumbsup:
